title: Art & Archaeology
lede: An atlas of rock art, sacred monumental architecture, museum collections and living creative traditions across Africa.

path.title: Path: signs in the landscape across millennia
path.intro: Follow seven places from prehistoric marks in stone to Kushite pyramids, medieval stone citadels, royal bas-reliefs, and modern painting workshops. Put them in chronological order.
path.prompt: Put these stops in historical sequence: from the oldest rock art to modern institutions.

items.text: Painted rock shelters preserve pastoral figures of cattle and people in Somaliland.
Kushite pyramids and temples develop distinct Nubian architectural and relief traditions.
Granite dry-stone enclosures rise alongside royal soapstone bird sculptures.
Sudano-Sahelian monumental earthen architecture flourishes with mason guild traditions.
Fon rulers commission polychrome clay bas-reliefs and royal appliqué tapestries.
A painting workshop in Brazzaville pioneers modern African easel painting.
Post-independence national gallery preserves and displays Namibian and African visual arts.

categories.label: Rock art and archaeology
categories.intro: Marks in stone, petroglyphs, megaliths and ancient landscapes that preserve thousands of years of human imagery, pastoral life and ritual presence.

categories.label: Monumental & sacred architecture
categories.intro: Monolithic stone churches, Sudano-Sahelian earthen masterworks, dry-stone citadels and royal palaces where architecture acts as sculpture and cultural record.

categories.label: Museums, galleries & archives
categories.intro: Public institutions where historical collections, modern fine arts, photography and world-class archives are cared for, interpreted and made accessible.

categories.label: Living practices, studios & workshops
categories.intro: Living performance traditions, historic artist workshops, sacred groves and artist communities where culture continues to be made, taught and reinvented.
